example.name: ecommerce_checkout_usability
example.description: Complete usability test for e-commerce checkout process

context.business_problem: High cart abandonment rate (68%) during checkout
context.research_objective: Identify usability issues causing abandonment and recommend improvements
context.timeline: 3 weeks from planning to final report
context.resources: UX researcher, 8 participants, prototype, analytics data

actions.action: Defined success metrics: completion rate, time on task, error rate, satisfaction
Created task scenarios: guest checkout, registered user checkout, payment methods
Recruited 8 participants: 4 new users, 4 returning customers
Prepared test environment with prototype and analytics tracking

deliverables.deliverable: Research plan with objectives and methodology

actions.action: Conducted 8 individual usability testing sessions
Collected think-aloud protocols and screen recordings
Measured task completion times and error rates
Administered System Usability Scale (SUS) post-test

data_collected.metric: Average time on task: 8 minutes 45 seconds

actions.action: Analyzed screen recordings for common failure points
Identified recurring themes from think-aloud protocols
Correlated findings with existing analytics data
Prioritized issues by impact and frequency

key_findings.finding: Payment form confusion - 75% of users struggled with credit card format
Hidden shipping costs - 62% abandoned when costs revealed late
Account creation pressure - 50% of guest users frustrated by prompts
Mobile usability issues - 38% of mobile users had form input problems

actions.action: Created comprehensive research report with evidence
Developed prioritized recommendation matrix
Presented findings to product and engineering teams
Created implementation roadmap with success metrics

recommendations.recommendation: Show shipping costs earlier in checkout flow
Improve payment form validation and formatting
Optimize mobile form inputs and layouts

outcomes.outcome: Cart abandonment rate reduced to 45% (33% improvement)

example.name: saas_onboarding_research
example.description: Mixed-methods research to improve SaaS product onboarding

context.business_problem: 40% of new users drop off during first week
context.research_objective: Understand onboarding challenges and design improved experience
context.resources: UX researcher, product manager, 15 participants, analytics access

actions.action: Analyzed existing analytics to identify drop-off points
Reviewed support tickets from new users
Defined research questions: Why do users drop off? What are key success factors?
Planned mixed-methods approach: interviews + analytics + surveys
Conducted 12 in-depth interviews with recent users (6 retained, 6 churned)
Deployed onboarding satisfaction survey to 500 new users
Set up behavioral tracking for 50 new user cohorts
Collected product documentation and support content

data_collected.metric: Key drop-off point: Day 3 (35% of users)
Support tickets from new users: 28% of total volume

actions.action: Thematic analysis of interview transcripts
Statistical analysis of survey responses
Behavioral pattern analysis from tracking data
Developed 3 user personas based on research findings

key_findings.finding: Value proposition unclear - 60% don't understand key benefits
Complex setup process - 45% overwhelmed by configuration options
Lack of quick wins - 70% don't achieve meaningful outcome in first session
Poor help resources - 55% can't find answers when stuck

personas_created.persona: "Confused Explorer" - Needs guidance and clear value
"Efficiency Seeker" - Wants quick setup and immediate results
"Power User" - Needs advanced features and customization

actions.action: Created detailed onboarding journey maps for each persona
Identified critical moments and intervention points
Developed persona-specific onboarding flows
Created implementation roadmap with A/B test plan

recommendations.recommendation: Implement progressive disclosure based on user goals
Create interactive tutorials for key features
Design quick-win scenarios for first session

outcomes.outcome: New onboarding flow increased week-1 retention by 35%
Time-to-first-value reduced from 45 minutes to 15 minutes
Support tickets from new users decreased by 40%
User satisfaction with onboarding improved to 4.3/5.0

example.name: mobile_app_feature_validation
example.description: Research to validate new mobile app feature concepts

context.business_need: Validate feature ideas before development investment
context.research_objective: Assess user needs and preferences for 3 proposed features
context.resources: UX researcher, product designer, 20 participants, concept mockups

actions.action: Reviewed existing user research and feedback
Created low-fidelity mockups for 3 feature concepts
Developed concept description sheets
Planned concept testing methodology

feature_concepts.feature: Social Sharing - Enhanced sharing and collaboration features
Offline Mode - Access core features without internet

actions.action: Conducted 20 individual concept testing sessions
Used Kano model to assess feature satisfaction
Measured perceived value and willingness to pay
Collected feature ranking and prioritization data
Analyzed feature preferences across user segments
Calculated feature value scores and ROI estimates
Identified must-have vs nice-to-have features
Assessed technical feasibility and development effort

feature.name: Smart Recommendations
feature.value: High perceived value, willing to pay premium

feature.name: Social Sharing
feature.value: Medium perceived value, limited willingness to pay

feature.name: Offline Mode
feature.value: High perceived value for specific segments

actions.action: Created feature prioritization matrix
Developed phased implementation roadmap
Defined success metrics for each feature
Presented findings to product leadership

recommendations.recommendation: Phase 2: Implement basic Offline Mode for core features
Phase 3: Add Social Sharing features based on user feedback
Conduct A/B tests for feature adoption and usage

outcomes.outcome: Smart Recommendations feature achieved 40% adoption in first month
User engagement increased by 25% with personalized content
Development resources focused on highest-impact features
Feature validation saved 3 months of development on low-value features

example.name: accessibility_research
example.description: Comprehensive accessibility audit and user research

context.compliance_need: Ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance and improve accessibility
context.research_objective: Identify accessibility barriers and validate solutions with users with disabilities
context.timeline: 6 weeks for comprehensive audit and user testing
context.resources: UX researcher, accessibility expert, 12 users with disabilities, audit tools

actions.action: Conducted automated accessibility testing with multiple tools
Performed manual keyboard navigation testing
Reviewed color contrast and visual design
Assessed screen reader compatibility

audit_findings.finding: Major issues: keyboard navigation, form labels, color contrast
Screen reader compatibility problems with dynamic content

actions.action: Recruited 12 users with diverse disabilities
Conducted usability testing with assistive technologies
Observed task completion with screen readers, keyboard-only, voice control
Collected qualitative feedback on accessibility barriers

participant_profile.profile: 2 users with low vision (magnification, high contrast)

actions.action: Triangulated audit findings with user testing results
Prioritized issues by impact on user experience
Collaborated with designers on accessibility solutions
Developed accessibility guidelines and standards

key_insights.insight: Automated tools caught only 60% of real accessibility barriers
Screen reader users struggled most with dynamic content updates
Keyboard navigation issues prevented task completion for many users
Color contrast problems affected users with low vision significantly

actions.action: Created detailed accessibility improvement roadmap
Implemented high-priority fixes first
Conducted validation testing with users with disabilities
Established ongoing accessibility testing process

improvements_made.improvement: Added comprehensive ARIA labels and landmarks
Improved color contrast to WCAG AA standards
Added skip links and focus management

outcomes.outcome: Achieved WCAG 2.1 AA compliance across the application
Task completion rate for users with disabilities increased from 35% to 85%
Established accessibility testing as part of standard development process

example.name: executive_summary
example.title: E-commerce Checkout Usability Research - Executive Summary
example.content:
## Key Findings - 68% cart abandonment due to usability issues - Primary barrier: Hidden shipping costs revealed too late - Payment form confusion affects 75% of users
## Business Impact - Potential revenue increase: $2.3M annually - Implementation cost: $150K - Expected ROI: 1,433% within 6 months
## Top Recommendations 1. Show shipping costs early (Impact: High, Effort: Low) 2. Improve payment form validation (Impact: High, Effort: Medium) 3. Make account creation optional (Impact: Medium, Effort: Low)
## Next Steps - Implement high-priority fixes within 4 weeks - A/B test new checkout flow - Measure impact on conversion rate

example.name: research_insight
example.title: User Insight: Payment Form Confusion
example.content:
**Observation:** 6 out of 8 participants struggled with credit card input format
**Interpretation:** Users expect automatic formatting and real-time validation
**Implication:** Current form creates friction and abandonment during critical conversion moment
**Recommendation:** Implement auto-formatting and inline validation for payment forms
**Confidence:** High (multiple data points, clear pattern)
**Evidence:** - Interview #3: "I don't know if I'm entering this right" - Interview #7: "The format is confusing, should include spaces" - Analytics: 45% form abandonment at payment step
